title: Prenatal and childhood infections as risk factors for psychiatric disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis
title_zh: 孕期与儿童期感染作为精神障碍风险因素的系统综述与Meta分析
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To perform a systematic review and meta-analysis of the associations between infections during the prenatal period or childhood and the risk of subsequent psychiatric disorders (including ADHD, ASD, internalising and psychotic disorders) considering timing (prenatal and childhood), type (bacterial vs viral), and trimester of infection. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed and ProQuest was conducted from 20 May 2024-15 July 2025 for cohort studies reporting psychiatric outcomes following infection exposure during pregnancy or childhood (0≤12 years). Study quality was assessed using the STROBE checklist. Where possible, random-effects meta-analyses were conducted using logarithmic risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals. RESULTS: Seventy-five studies were included in the review, with 59 contributing to meta-analyses. Prenatal infection was associated with increased risk of ADHD (RR = 1.18; 95% CI: 1.07-1.31), ASD (RR = 1.17; 95% CI: 1.07-1.28), and psychotic disorders (RR = 1.21; 95% CI: 1.13-1.29). Childhood infection was also associated with ADHD (RR = 1.45; 95% CI: 1.27-1.66), ASD (RR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.26-1.59), and psychosis (RR = 1.31; 95% CI: 1.07-1.60). Subgroup analyses indicated prenatal bacterial infections were associated with ADHD and ASD, while prenatal viral infections; particularly during the first-trimester, were linked to psychotic disorders. Childhood bacterial infections were also associated with ADHD and ASD. Too few studies were available to conduct meta-analyses for internalising disorders. CONCLUSION: Early-life infection is associated with increased risk of multiple psychiatric outcomes. These findings support a role for immune activation during critical developmental periods in shaping later psychiatric risk.
abstract_zh: OBJECTIVES：系统综述并Meta分析产前或儿童期感染与后续精神障碍风险（包括ADHD、ASD、内化性障碍和精神病性障碍）的关联，考虑感染时点（产前与童年）、类型（细菌与病毒）及妊娠孕期。METHODS：我们在PubMed和ProQuest中进行了系统检索，检索范围为2024年5月20日—2025年7月15日，纳入报告妊娠期或儿童期（0≤12岁）感染暴露后精神结局的队列研究。采用STROBE清单评估研究质量。可行时，采用随机效应Meta分析并使用对数风险比（log risk ratio）及95%置信区间。RESULTS：综述纳入75项研究，其中59项参与Meta分析。产前感染与ADHD（RR = 1.18；95% CI: 1.07–1.31）、ASD（RR = 1.17；95% CI: 1.07–1.28）以及精神病性障碍（RR = 1.21；95% CI: 1.13–1.29）的风险均升高。儿童期感染也与ADHD（RR = 1.45；95% CI: 1.27–1.66）、ASD（RR = 1.41；95% CI: 1.26–1.59）及精神病性障碍（RR = 1.31；95% CI: 1.07–1.60）相关。亚组分析显示，产前细菌感染与ADHD、ASD相关，而产前病毒感染，尤其在第一孕期，与精神病性障碍相关。儿童细菌感染也与ADHD和ASD相关。用于内化性障碍的Meta分析可纳入研究过少。CONCLUSION：早期生活感染与多种精神结局风险升高相关。上述结果支持在关键发育阶段免疫激活参与塑造后续精神疾病风险。
